key_insight: Out-of-the-box tabular foundation models are highly competitive Bayesian optimization surrogates for materials discovery, without task-specific training or Gaussian process kernel selection.
engineering_relevance: TabPFN and TabICL could reduce surrogate-model configuration effort in materials active learning workflows.
method: Use TabPFN and TabICL as out-of-the-box surrogate models.
Evaluate on two standard materials science benchmarks.
Compare against Gaussian processes, random forests, and CatBoost.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports highly competitive performance across two benchmarks but provides no numerical results.
watch_item: Performance beyond the two evaluated benchmarks remains unestablished.
paper_title: Out-of-the-Box Tabular Foundation Models for Bayesian Optimization in Materials Discovery
